title: Are NMN Supplements Safe To Take? Learn More About NMN
abstract:
# Are NMN Supplements Safe?  
As we age, our bodies become less efficient at [breaking down nutrients](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5227979/) for energy production. Our cells begin to divide and work more slowly, affecting the way our organs function and fight off diseases.  
Good sleep habits, regular exercise, and a healthy diet can [slow aging effects](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4340807/) and [increase our life span](https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pmed.1003889). That said, some supplements can give these practices an even bigger boost.  
One of the most promising so far is the anti-aging molecule NMN. Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) has been shown to [prevent metabolic disorders](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35076274/) and [reduce inflammation](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7238909/), both in animal studies and in healthy adults. But are NMN supplements safe to take?  
In this article, we’ll take a closer look at NMN supplements. Read on to find out what their benefits and risks are, and if they’re safe to take for warding off age-related complications.
## What Are NMN Supplements?  
[NMN supplements](https://rtmedusa.com/product/nmn-powder/) are a popular, heavily regulated therapeutic drug made with nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN). NMN is a naturally occurring nucleotide that is derived from niacin, a.k.a. vitamin B3.  
Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) is a precursor of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD). NAD is key to many bodily functions because it regulates many cellular pathways, [gene expression](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29309893/), and [cellular energy metabolism](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2212877821000351).  
However, as people get older, their [production of NAD precursors](https://jbiomedsci.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12929-019-0527-8) like NMN goes down. This lowers NAD levels in human tissue, causing slower cell growth and age-related physiological decline. Production of NAD precursors can go down by as much as half by the time an adult reaches their fifties, leading to age-related conditions like brain fog, [skeletal muscle aging](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4985182/), and even [Alzheimer’s disease](https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fcell.2021.668491/full).
### Store Your Anti-Aging Supplements Correctly  
Always keep your NMN supplements in a cool, dry place out of reach of children or in your fridge. High temperatures or exposure to moisture can cause nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) to degrade. When it breaks down into nicotinamide, it can cause headaches, nausea, and liver toxicity. Keeping your anti-aging supplements in good condition will ensure that they’re safe for consumption.
